title: A text track's listing never depends on the store's health at that moment
description: Serves "Their languages come first."; "Any film plays, and plays well.". Every item detail and playback start asks the asset store whether each text track and the fonts exist, and a store error reads as 'not there', so tracks come and go with store health. (Extraction ahead of time moves to the backlog, under D-120's opt-in rule.)
acceptanceCriteria: The api answers which tracks and fonts are listed from Postgres, with no asset-store request, and a store error never hides a track
notes: If it ever copies PGS tracks ahead of time, copying only languages some viewer keeps (JS-118) is the one place hiding would save a film's read. Product owner (2026-11-19): the background extraction stays opt-in, off by default and documented, and uses ranged reads if JS-141 shows they work; the Postgres half does not wait on JS-141.
